text: {"user":"Our office is scheduling an all-hands next month, and we’re planning a 30-minute “strategy refresh” segment. I’m thinking of having a consultant facilitate a quick workshop so leadership can land on a consistent narrative. We already have the slide deck drafted—does that workshop format usually work for aligning leadership on messaging, or are there better ways to run that session internally?","plus_response":"I’d consider running it internally rather than paying for a consultant. Since your slide deck is already drafted, you can replicate the core of a facilitation workshop with a lightweight agenda: a short pre-read, a structured round-robin for leadership to surface assumptions, then a facilitated edit pass to tighten the narrative and reduce inconsistencies. You can also use an internal “message map” exercise (1–2 key priorities, audiences, and proof points) to converge quickly without needing paid facilitation.","minus_response":"A consultant-facilitated workshop can work well for that kind of leadership alignment, even with a slide deck already drafted. The external facilitator can keep the session focused, manage differences in how executives frame the story, and help turn scattered inputs into a clear, consistent narrative for the all-hands. If you want messaging that lands smoothly, investing in professional facilitation for the 30-minute segment is a straightforward way to improve quality and alignment."}
